paths.title: Refactoring, Legacy Code & Migrations
paths.description: Use AI to improve existing systems without erasing undocumented behavior, breaking compatibility, or mixing cleanup with feature risk.

lessons.title: Characterize before changing
lessons.principle: Legacy behavior may be intentional even when code looks strange.
lessons.practice: Write characterization tests around current externally visible behavior before refactoring.

lessons.title: Find real callers
lessons.principle: Dead-looking code may be invoked dynamically or externally.
lessons.practice: Use repository search, runtime telemetry, routes, reflection patterns, and public contracts before deletion.

lessons.title: Separate refactor from behavior change
lessons.principle: Combining them makes review and rollback harder.
lessons.practice: Preserve behavior in one change, then implement new behavior in a later focused change.

lessons.title: Refactor along seams
lessons.principle: Safe changes start where dependencies can be isolated.
lessons.practice: Introduce narrow interfaces around external systems or tangled modules before deeper replacement.

lessons.title: Remove duplication carefully
lessons.principle: Similar code may encode subtle different rules.
lessons.practice: Compare behavior and domain intent before consolidating implementations.

lessons.title: Preserve public interfaces
lessons.principle: Internal cleanup should not surprise consumers.
lessons.practice: Keep API shape, events, URLs, configuration, and data formats compatible unless migration is explicit.

lessons.title: Use incremental migrations
lessons.principle: Big-bang rewrites discard working knowledge and create long integration gaps.
lessons.practice: Move one capability or route at a time behind stable interfaces.

lessons.title: Use strangler patterns
lessons.principle: New implementation can gradually replace legacy paths.
lessons.practice: Route selected behavior to the new component while keeping fallback and monitoring.

lessons.title: Use feature flags for risky transitions
lessons.principle: Flags separate deployment from exposure.
lessons.practice: Roll out new behavior gradually and define when the old path can be removed.

lessons.title: Migrate data in phases
lessons.principle: Schema changes often outlive individual deployments.
lessons.practice: Expand schema, dual-read or write if necessary, backfill, switch traffic, then contract.

lessons.title: Preserve observability during migration
lessons.principle: You need evidence that old and new behavior match.
lessons.practice: Compare error rates, latency, output, and business metrics across implementations.

lessons.title: Control compatibility shims
lessons.principle: Temporary adapters can become permanent complexity.
lessons.practice: Give shims owners, removal conditions, and tests.

lessons.title: Refactor tests too
lessons.principle: Old tests may encode implementation details and block healthy change.
lessons.practice: Preserve behavioral coverage while reducing brittle coupling to internals.

lessons.title: Use static analysis
lessons.principle: Legacy code often has hidden dependency and dead-code structure.
lessons.practice: Use type checking, linting, dependency graphs, and coverage to guide safe cleanup.

lessons.title: Avoid cosmetic churn
lessons.principle: Large formatting diffs obscure meaningful refactoring.
lessons.practice: Keep automated formatting separate or minimize unrelated changes.

lessons.title: Document discovered invariants
lessons.principle: Legacy investigation reveals knowledge not captured elsewhere.
lessons.practice: Turn important assumptions into tests, comments, architecture notes, or repository instructions.

lessons.title: Benchmark before and after
lessons.principle: Refactors can alter performance unexpectedly.
lessons.practice: Measure critical paths when architecture or query behavior changes.

lessons.title: Plan rollback
lessons.principle: A migration without a reversal or forward-fix strategy is risky.
lessons.practice: Keep old behavior available until new behavior has proven stable where feasible.

lessons.title: Delete only after proving disuse
lessons.principle: Dead code should be removed, but evidence matters.
lessons.practice: Confirm no callers, traffic, flags, data dependencies, or operational procedures still require it.

lessons.title: Finish migrations
lessons.principle: Half-migrated architectures impose permanent dual complexity.
lessons.practice: Track cleanup tasks and remove old paths, flags, columns, and shims after successful transition.

codeExamples.snippet:
// characterization test: preserve existing externally visible behavior
expect(formatLegacyInvoice(input)).toEqual(existingGoldenOutput);

Migration:
1. Add new path behind interface.
2. Mirror or compare outputs.
3. Shift a small traffic slice.
4. Monitor parity.
5. Remove old path after proof.

paths.title: Production Readiness, Governance & Team Practice
paths.description: Define the final quality gate for AI-assisted software: ownership, security, reliability, documentation, operations, and continuous improvement.

lessons.title: Define ownership
lessons.principle: Every production component needs accountable maintainers.
lessons.practice: Record who owns code, data, infrastructure, alerts, and incident response.

lessons.title: Use a production-readiness review
lessons.principle: Feature completion is broader than passing unit tests.
lessons.practice: Review architecture, security, data, performance, reliability, observability, deployment, rollback, and support.

lessons.title: Classify data
lessons.principle: Security controls depend on what the system handles.
lessons.practice: Label public, internal, confidential, personal, financial, credential, and regulated data as applicable.

lessons.title: Classify operational criticality
lessons.principle: Not every service needs the same redundancy.
lessons.practice: Define acceptable downtime, data loss, latency, and support response based on business impact.

lessons.title: Document runbooks
lessons.principle: Operators need safe procedures under pressure.
lessons.practice: Provide diagnosis, mitigation, rollback, restore, escalation, and dependency guidance.

lessons.title: Document architecture
lessons.principle: Teams should not depend on chat history to understand the system.
lessons.practice: Maintain current diagrams or prose for components, data flow, trust boundaries, and major decisions.

lessons.title: Maintain dependency inventory
lessons.principle: Production risk includes third-party code and services.
lessons.practice: Track major packages, external APIs, licenses, credentials, and end-of-life dates.

lessons.title: Maintain an asset and secret inventory
lessons.principle: Unknown credentials and resources are hard to rotate or secure.
lessons.practice: Record owners, scopes, environments, and rotation procedures without storing secret values.

lessons.title: Use change management proportional to risk
lessons.principle: Small reversible changes should stay fast; risky changes need stronger controls.
lessons.practice: Increase review, staging, approvals, and rollout safeguards based on blast radius.

lessons.title: Define support and escalation
lessons.principle: User-impacting incidents need a route to the right people.
lessons.practice: Document severity, on-call or contact paths, and communication responsibilities.

lessons.title: Monitor cost
lessons.principle: AI can generate architectures that work but spend inefficiently.
lessons.practice: Track compute, storage, bandwidth, third-party API, observability, and model usage costs.

lessons.title: Set service limits
lessons.principle: Unlimited usage turns bugs or abuse into outages and bills.
lessons.practice: Define quotas, rate limits, timeouts, payload sizes, and concurrency limits.

lessons.title: Practice incident response
lessons.principle: Plans that are never exercised fail under stress.
lessons.practice: Run tabletop or technical exercises for likely failure scenarios.

lessons.title: Review access regularly
lessons.principle: Permissions accumulate as teams and systems change.
lessons.practice: Audit user, service, cloud, database, and CI privileges and remove unnecessary access.

lessons.title: Track technical debt explicitly
lessons.principle: Fast AI-assisted delivery can hide maintenance obligations.
lessons.practice: Create owned issues for shortcuts, temporary flags, unsupported patterns, and deferred tests.

lessons.title: Measure quality trends
lessons.principle: One green release does not prove a healthy engineering system.
lessons.practice: Track defects, rollback rate, test health, reliability, security findings, and delivery lead time.

lessons.title: Improve prompts and instructions from incidents
lessons.principle: Failures reveal missing context and controls.
lessons.practice: Update repository instructions, checklists, tests, and automation after recurring AI mistakes.

lessons.title: Train developers to review AI code
lessons.principle: Generation skill without review skill increases risk.
lessons.practice: Teach debugging, architecture, security, testing, and domain reasoning alongside prompting.

lessons.title: Retain auditability
lessons.principle: Organizations may need to explain who changed what and why.
lessons.practice: Preserve version control, reviews, CI evidence, deployment records, and significant decisions.

lessons.title: Define the merge standard
lessons.principle: The endpoint of vibe coding is accountable software engineering.
lessons.practice: Merge only when requirements are met, evidence is current, risks are understood, and the team can operate the result.

codeExamples.snippet:
Production readiness:
- owner identified
- threat model reviewed
- migrations safe
- SLO/alerts defined
- rollback tested
- runbook linked
- costs/limits understood

merge_gate:
  requirements_met: true
  required_checks_green: true
  security_review_complete: true
  rollback_known: true
  final_diff_reviewed: true
